lyrics:
[Intro: fingerpicked acoustic guitar, soft hum]

[Verse 1: quiet, gentle, close]
For a while there it was rough
I'll be honest, I'd had enough
Now there's coffee on at six
And a kid who's learning tricks
And my mother calls to laugh
And you sleep on my bad half

[Pre-Chorus: guitar strums harder, voice rising]
And I know how these things go
I've seen a good thing overthrown

[Chorus: explosive, full rock band, roared]
So don't move a thing
Leave it, leave it like it is
If there's somebody keeping count
I'm asking, I'm asking
Let me keep the lot
It's too good to hold
And it's all I've got

[Verse 2: quiet again, a little shaken]
Got a roof and a garden bed
Got a calm inside my head
And I catch myself at night
Checking every lock and light
'Cause the best that I have known
Has a way of being loaned

[Pre-Chorus: guitar strums harder, voice rising]
And I know how these things go
I've seen a good thing overthrown

[Chorus: explosive, full rock band, roared]
So don't move a thing
Leave it, leave it like it is
If there's somebody keeping count
I'm asking, I'm asking
Let me keep the lot
It's too good to hold
And it's all I've got

[Bridge: band pounding, wordless yelps, building]
Oh, oh-oh
Please
Oh, oh-oh
Please

[Final Chorus: loudest, voice at the top of its range]
So don't move a thing
Leave it, leave it like it is
If there's somebody keeping count
I'm asking, I'm asking
Let me keep the lot

[Outro: sudden quiet, acoustic guitar, almost spoken]
It's too good to hold
I'm holding it
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 105 BPM with a lilting, swaying feel, B-flat major. Hushed folk that detonates into arena rock.

VOICE: Male tenor with a very wide range. Verses are soft, warm and close with a slight tremble. The chorus is roared from the chest at the top of his range, with a rough edge and a yelp on the high notes. Wordless yelps in the bridge. The last two lines are nearly spoken.

INSTRUMENTS: A fingerpicked acoustic guitar. Then, all at once, loud overdriven electric guitars, pounding live drums with crashing cymbals, and a driving bass. Piano doubling the chords. A soft hum of backing voices. The band drops out completely for the last lines.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, acoustic guitar. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:38 Pre-chorus. 0:48 Chorus 1, the band explodes in. 1:14 Verse 2, quiet again. 1:42 Pre-chorus. 1:52 Chorus 2. 2:18 Bridge, pounding with yelps. 2:34 Final chorus, loudest. 2:54 Outro, sudden quiet, guitar and two near-spoken lines at 3:06.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-2020s folk-rock built for a dramatic clip: the verse dry and intimate, the chorus huge, wide and slightly distorted, the contrast as large as possible.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first word of the first chorus at 0:48, when the whole band arrives at once.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The fear that good things are 'loaned' belongs to someone who has already lost a few. The last line answers the title: it is too good to hold, and he is holding it anyway.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Gratitude, dread, pleading, a steady hand.
